propositions: New hard-fail CI gates are landing ungrandfathered, breaking branches created before the gate was added, because code-review has no criterion checking whether a pre-gate branch would now fail.

The proposed solution is a new advisory `project.ci-gate-compat` criterion routed by declarative `applies_to` glob patterns matching CI config files across multiple vendors, never hardcoded to a specific CI system.

Project criteria must be gated on their `applies_to` globs against changed files, and the glob set must be overridable via a config key `[code_review] ci_config_globs` so unusual pipelines are declared rather than enumerated.

The implementation requires core changes to dispatch semantics in `gate_dispatch.py` and `registry.py` to filter activated project criteria by their effective globs, impacting all project code-review criteria not just the new one.
This ticket was rejected by operator decision: the remedy for a gate failure is rebase-and-fix, not a compatibility mechanism that institutionalizes working around gate failures.
The salvageable core fix—making `applies_to` actually gate project code-review criteria—was separated as a conditional follow-up to be filed independently if confirmed as a pre-existing defect.
